tasks.short: Hear about home and environment risks, look up local data, write and send letters to landlords, and raise issues with the public health service.

steps.what: Nurse practitioner hears about home and environmental health risks from patients in consults
Nurse practitioner looks up local air and water data on public websites
Nurse practitioner records the patient's consent to name them and their home in the letter
Nurse practitioner writes letters to housing corporations about a patient's unhealthy home
Nurse practitioner checks the final letter: the facts about the home and the health problem, the local data, the consent and the housing corporation's address
Nurse practitioner signs the checked letter and releases it to the housing corporation: posted by hand today, through the practice's mail service after the change
Nurse practitioner advocates for accessible care in meetings with the public health service and municipality

tasks.design: A saved view of public air and water data for the practice's postcode areas ({GOV_PORTAL}) replaces the search per case. A letter template fills the patient's details (with consent), the health problem and the local data; the practitioner records the patient's consent, writes the case, checks the final letter and the address and signs it once; the practice's mail service then sends it. Hearing patients and speaking up in meetings stay with the practitioner.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each case meant a new search and a letter from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Public bodies publish environmental data by location, and letter templates fill from the record.
tasks.still_hard: Landlords and councils respond to persistence, not letters alone.
tasks.human_edge: Speaking up credibly for a family in a damp flat.

reach.learn: Whether shared templates speed up landlord responses.

evidence.claim: Public bodies publish air quality and water data by location.
Sharing a patient's health details with a landlord needs the patient's explicit consent; health data are special category.

assumptions: Boundary: from patients' reports to issues raised; policy decisions by the municipality are outside.
Input contract: public data sources chosen by the practitioner; letter template set by the practice's medical staff; patient consent recorded in the record; fallback is a letter from scratch.

Hearing patients, recording consent, the final check and meetings keep their full time; asking consent before writing about a patient is needed today as well. s2 keeps 50 because the saved view replaces the search but the practitioner still reads the data for the case; s3 keeps 75 because the template fills details and data and the practitioner writes the case; s4 keeps 25 for signing and releasing the letter.
research_questions: Do landlords respond sooner to letters with local data?

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep for the practitioner: the medical staff keep the letter template and the saved view needs no care; consent is recorded in s2k.

approvals.approved_version: The letter exactly as checked by the practitioner in s3c, signed and sent once to the housing corporation at the address checked there; any change needs a new check and signature.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the saved view lacks data for half of the cases (s2 keeps 75) and most letters are written from scratch (s3 keeps 90) (8.6); high: the view and template work as designed (15.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Hear what help is needed, search for services, phone to check availability, send the chosen contacts and help with applications.

steps.what: Nurse practitioner hears what help the patient or caregivers need
Nurse practitioner searches websites and a paper list for suitable health care resources
Nurse practitioner phones services to check they can take the patient
Nurse practitioner checks the final contact list: the services chosen after the calls, their details, and that it goes to this patient

Nurse practitioner gives the patient the chosen contacts: written on a note today; picked from the directory and sent once through the patient portal after the change, printed for patients without the portal
Nurse practitioner helps the caregiver with applications for home care or aids

tasks.design: A local service directory in the electronic health record ({OTHER}) lists home care, therapists, support groups and aids by type, area and insurer contract, kept current by the practice assistant; the practitioner filters it instead of searching. After the calls the practitioner picks the chosen services from the directory, checks the final list and sends it once to the patient through the patient portal; patients without the portal get a printout. Hearing needs, phoning services and helping with applications stay with the practitioner.
tasks.previous_blocker: Services were found through web searches and an outdated paper list.
tasks.enabler_now: A simple records app can hold a filtered service directory, and patient portals send messages.
tasks.still_hard: Directories go stale; waiting lists change weekly.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which service will suit this caregiver.

reach.task: Answer patients' questions on local services
reach.learn: Whether one directory serves the whole practice.

evidence.claim: A simple records app can hold a service directory filtered by type, area and contract.
Health data are special category; sending contacts through the portal keeps them out of e-mail.

assumptions: Boundary: from the need to the application; the services themselves are outside.
Input contract: directory entries kept by the practice assistant; insurer contracts from the insurers' lists; fallback is web search.
Assistant time is outside the practitioner's savings.

Hearing, phoning, the final check and helping keep their full time. s2 keeps 40 because the practitioner filters the directory and reads the results; s4 keeps 25 for picking the services, the send and printouts.
unknowns: Directory entries needed for the area.
research_questions: Do patients reach a service sooner?

already_counted.description: Nurse practitioner reviews the filtered results.

incremental.description: Practice assistant keeps the directory current.

approvals.approved_version: The list of chosen services with their contact details exactly as checked by the practitioner in s4c, sent once to this patient's portal inbox or printed for that patient; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the directory misses many unusual needs (s2 keeps 70) and half of the patients have no portal (s4 keeps 60) (11.1); high: the directory covers most needs and most patients use the portal (21.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read insurers' yearly policies, check authorisation per patient, phone insurers on unclear cases, attend contract meetings and brief colleagues.

steps.what: Nurse practitioner reads each insurer's yearly purchasing and reimbursement policy for payer systems changes

loop.input: Each insurer's yearly purchasing and reimbursement policy documents.
loop.output: A table per insurer of the rules that apply to the practice's care (prior authorisation, referral needs, covered services), each cell quoting its passage and page.
loop.check: Code checks every quoted passage appears word for word in the current policy. A second check reads each cell against its passage and flags cells the passage does not support; the practitioner verifies each changed or flagged cell against the passage and reads the policy in full where no passage settles it.
loop.stop: One run per policy version; cells without a passage stay empty.
loop.why_not_simpler: Policies differ in structure per insurer; fixed text search misses rules worded differently.

steps.what: Nurse practitioner checks per patient whether the insurer needs prior authorisation: by looking it up today, by reading the flag in the record after the change
Nurse practitioner phones insurers about unclear cases
Nurse practitioner attends regional meetings on insurer contracts and regulatory processes
Nurse practitioner briefs colleagues on changes in the team meeting

tasks.design: Each year a bounded step extracts the rules that matter to the practice from every insurer's policy documents ({PARTNER_PORTAL}) into one table, each cell quoting its passage; the practitioner verifies changed cells. The electronic health record ({OTHER}) uses the verified table to show, per patient's insurer, whether prior authorisation is needed. Phoning insurers, meetings and briefing colleagues stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each insurer's policy was read in full and rules checked per patient by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Insurers publish yearly policies, and language models can extract rules with quoted passages.
tasks.still_hard: Policies change mid-year; a wrong flag can mean an unpaid claim.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which insurer contact will give a straight answer.
tasks.altitude: The practitioner verifies extracted rules instead of reading every policy.

reach.learn: Whether one rule table cuts rejected claims.

evidence.claim: Insurers publish yearly purchasing and reimbursement policies.
Providers are responsible for careful use of generative AI: assess risks, test and monitor.

assumptions: Boundary: from insurer policies to a briefed team; contract negotiation is outside.
Input contract: policy documents published by each insurer; patient insurer recorded at registration by the practice assistant; fallback is reading in full.
Phoning, meetings and briefing keep their full time. s1 keeps 50 for verifying changed cells; s2 keeps 10 for reading the flag and looking up insurers the table does not cover.
No patient data go into the extraction.
research_questions: Do rejected claims for missing authorisation fall?

already_counted.description: Nurse practitioner verifies changed cells in the table.

incremental.description: Nurse practitioner reports wrong authorisation flags.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the extraction misses many rules, so reading keeps 75 and the flag covers few patients (s2 keeps 40) (19.0); high: the table covers the practice's insurers (32.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assign tasks in the huddle, see open tasks, guide staff, co-sign their care and chase overdue tasks.

steps.what: Nurse practitioner assigns daily tasks to support staff in the morning huddle
Nurse practitioner records the huddle tasks with owner and due time: on a paper list today, in the record's task list after the change
Support staff mark their tasks done in the record's task list
Nurse practitioner checks paper lists and the record for open patient care tasks
Nurse practitioner guides support staff with questions during the day
Nurse practitioner reviews and co-signs care given by support staff
Nurse practitioner chases unfinished tasks: by message and phone today; after the change the record reminds the owner and the practitioner follows up tasks still overdue

tasks.design: Tasks agreed in the huddle go into the task list of the electronic health record ({OTHER}) with owner and due time, so the practitioner sees all open tasks in one view, and the record reminds the owner when a task is overdue. Support staff mark their tasks done, and the practitioner follows up tasks still overdue after the reminder. The huddle, guiding staff and co-signing care stay with the practitioner; task data are not used to rate staff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Open tasks were spread over paper lists and the record, and chasing was by message.
tasks.enabler_now: Record systems hold task lists with owners, due times and reminders.
tasks.still_hard: Tasks only show if staff enter them.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a new assistant is struggling and stepping in.

evidence.claim: Record systems hold task lists with owners, due times and reminders.
Task logs show staff performance; using them to monitor staff needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the huddle to finished tasks; staff appraisal is outside.
Input contract: tasks entered by the practitioner and support staff; task types set by the practice manager; fallback is paper lists.

The huddle, guiding and co-signing keep their full time; recording huddle tasks keeps its time because typing them replaces the paper list. s2 keeps 40 for reading the open-task view; s5 keeps 30 for following up tasks still overdue after the reminder.
Staff time entering tasks is outside the practitioner's savings.

incremental.description: Nurse practitioner moves owners and due times when tasks change during the day.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: staff do not keep the list current, so the paper check keeps 70 and chasing keeps 60 (8.0); high: tasks are entered and closed in the list (15.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The nurse practitioner keeps advocacy, guidance and decisions; searches, letters, policy reading and chasing shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A practitioner who knows each insurer's rules without reading every policy.
